title: Buckinghamshire Council: Early adoption of Microsoft Copilot
summary: Buckinghamshire reports that Copilot shortens call wrap-up and supports a deaf colleague in participating in meetings more independently.
account: Buckinghamshire reports that Copilot saves two minutes per customer-service call and 60–90 minutes daily for a monitored group of six executive assistants. A deaf colleague reportedly participates in meetings and reviews conversations with less assistance. The source does not establish whether that gain persisted. It also reports hallucinations and inconsistencies in other uses.
purpose: Support staff productivity and work quality through transcription, summarization, and drafting.
domain: Local government administration and workplace accessibility

ratings.reason: Reported call-wrap and executive-assistant task-time savings fit depth 1.
The specific colleague can follow speakers, review discussions, and check emails more independently. This supports improved capability without assuming documented lasting restoration.

ai_role.statement: The council attributes shorter call wrap-up and drafting tasks to Copilot. Its account also links the transcription functionality to a deaf colleague’s greater independence. The source does not isolate the contribution of each feature or training component.

evidence.citation: Local Government Association, AI case-study bank. Council or project account published by LGA. Hosting and editorial curation do not establish independent outcome evaluation.
evidence.title: Buckinghamshire Council: Early adoption of Microsoft Copilot

produced_by: The early-adopter rollout provided 300 licenses across departments, with staff support and monitoring of selected tasks.
The accessibility account concerns a specific colleague using transcription to identify speakers, review discussions, and track actions.
must_hold: The source does not establish which conditions are necessary to reproduce the reported benefit.

headline: Buckinghamshire reports time savings and better deaf access

revisions.change: Added the sourced case with separate benefit depth, beneficiary, evidence confidence, and outcome status assessments.

claim_basis: The deployer's report is on file. There is no independent source and no finding by a regulator or court.
